'Madden,' 'ESPN' Football Score in Different Ways. EA Sports would like to think absenteeism was high because Madden NFL 2005 came out, and some fans are rabid enough to take a sick day to play it.

Group to Propose New High-Speed Wireless Format. A group of technology companies including Texas Instruments, STMicroelectronics and Broadcom said they will propose a new wireless networking standard up to 10 times the speed of the current generation.

AOL to Sell Cheap PCs to Minorities and Seniors. America Online said it plans to sell a low-priced PC targeting low-income and minority households who agree to sign up for a year of dialup Internet service.
Companies Approve New High-Capacity Disc Format. A group of consumer electronics makers approved the format for a new generation of discs that can store five times the data of DVDs at the same cost.

Missing June Deals Slow to Return for Software Companies. The mystery of what went wrong for the software industry in late June when sales stalled at more than 20 brand-name companies is not even close to being solved.

Hacker Cracks Apple's Streaming Technology. The Norwegian hacker famed for developing DVD encryption-cracking software has apparently struck again, this time breaking the locks on Apple Computer's wireless music streaming technology.
European Download Services Go Mobile. The ability to download complete tracks directly over cell-phone networks to mobile phones is becoming a reality in Europe.
Oracle Sales Data Seen Being Released. Oracle Corp. sales documents detailing highly confidential information are likely to be made public, a federal judge said.
Sun's Looking Glass Provides 3D View. Developers get early code for new operating system 'skin' still being crafted.
Apple to open second Japanese retail store this month. Apple Computer Inc. will open its second Japanese retail store later this month in the western Japanese city of Osaka.
Charley's Force Took Experts by Surprise. Hurricane Charley's 145-mph force took forecasters by surprise and showed just how shaky a science it still is to predict a storm's intensity.

Science, Politics Collide in Election Year. With more than 4,000 scientists, including 48 Nobel Prize winners, having signed a statement opposing the Bush administration's use of scientific advice, this election year is seeing a new development.
Russian Cargo Craft Docks at Space Station. A Russian cargo ship docked with the international space station, bringing food, water, fuel and other items to the two-man Russian-American crew.

T. Rex Had Teen Growth Spurt, Scientists Say. Tyrannosaurus Rex grew incredibly fast during a teenaged growth spurt that saw the dinosaur expand its bulk by six times, but the fearsome beasts lived fast and died young.
Gene Blocker Turns Monkeys Into Workaholics. Procrastinating monkeys were turned into workaholics using a gene treatment to block a key brain compound, U.S. researchers reported.
Dolphins Too Have Born Socialites. Some people are born to be the life and soul of the party, and so it seems are some dolphins.

UK Scientists Allowed to Clone Human Embryos. British scientists said they had received permission to clone human embryos for medical research, in what they believe to be the first such license granted in Europe.

Russian Alien Spaceship Claims Raise Eyebrows, Skepticism. An expedition of Russian researchers claims to have found evidence that an alien spaceship had something to do with a huge explosion over Siberia in 1908.

Comets, Asteroids and Planets around a Nearby Star. A nearby star thought to harbor comets and asteroids now appears to be home to planets too. The presumed worlds are smaller than Jupiter and could be as tiny as Pluto.
Perseid Meteor Shower Peaks Overnight. A fine display of shooting stars is underway and peaks overnight. Astronomers expect the 2004 Perseid meteor shower to be one of the best in several years.

Redesigning Rockets: NASA Space Propulsion Finds a New Home. While the exploration of the Moon and other planets is exciting, the first task for astronauts and robots alike is to actually get to those destinations.

Studies Find Rats Can Get Hooked on Drugs. Rats can become drug addicts, scientists say. Now two studies by French and British researchers show the animals exhibit the same compulsive drive for cocaine as people do.
NASA Chief: Let's Go Save the Hubble. Amid uncertainty over the fate of the Hubble Space Telescope, NASA Administrator Sean O'Keefe gave the go-ahead for planning a robotic servicing mission.
Armadillo Aerospace's X Prize Prototype Crashes. Armadillo Aerospace of Mesquite, Texas has reported a crash last weekend of their prototype X Prize rocket.

Prairie Dog Won't Be on Endangered List. The black-tailed prairie dog has been dropped from a list of candidates for the federal endangered species list because scientists concluded the rodents are no longer threatened.
Hubble Trouble: One of Four Instruments Stops Working. One of the four astronomical instruments on the Hubble Space Telescope shut down and engineers are trying to pin down the problem.
Invasive Purple Weed May Meet Its Match. They burned it, mowed it, sprayed it and flooded it. But nothing killed the purple loosestrife weed until officials set a European beetle loose on it.

New NASA Supercomputer to Aid Theorists and Shuttle Engineers. NASA researchers have teamed up with Silicon Valley firms to build a supercomputer that ranks alongside the world's largest Linux-based systems.
Ants Form Supercolony Spanning 60 Miles. Normally clannish Argentine ants have become so laid back since arriving in Australia that they formed a supercolony spanning 60 miles, scientists say.
Rescuers Free Beached Whale in Brazil. Rescuers succeeded in freeing a minke whale that washed up on a beach in southeastern Brazil.
Red-Footed Falcon Sighted in Massachusetts. A red-footed falcon spotted for the first time in North America is enticing birdwatchers to Martha's Vineyard.
Weak Version of Most Powerful Explosions Found. Gamma-ray bursts are the most powerful events in the universe, temporarily outshining several galaxies and likely signaling the birth of a black hole.
Simultaneous Tropical Storms a Rarity. The prospect that a tropical storm and a hurricane could strike Florida on the same day is something meteorologists say they have never seen.
NASA's Genesis Spacecraft Adjusts Course. NASA's Genesis spacecraft successfully adjusted its course as it heads back toward Earth with a sample of solar wind particles.
Earth is Rare, New Study Suggests. Flip a coin. Heads, Earth is a common sort of planet. Tails, and ours is as unusual as a coin landing on edge.

Scientists Probe Pacific for Dead Zone. Using an array of scientific instruments, an Oregon State University graduate student probes the vibrant waters of the Pacific, searching for the absence of life.
Life on Mars Likely, Scientist Claims. Those twin robots hard at work on Mars have transmitted teasing views that reinforce the prospect that microbial life may exist on the red planet.
India Rethinks Plan to Send Man to Moon. India is rethinking its plan to send a man to the moon by 2015, as the mission would cost a lot of money and yield very little in return.
Natural Sunblock: Sun Dims in Strange Ways. When Venus crossed the Sun, astronomers noted something less obvious: the amount of sunlight reaching Earth dipped by 0.1 percent for a few hours.
Website Lets Users Scout the Red Planet from Home. NASA scientists have reformulated a website that lets the general public search data and images from previous Mars missions.
Britain Grants Human Cloning License. Britain granted its first license for human cloning, joining South Korea on the leading edge of stem cell research.
The Next Great Space Race. A piloted rocket ship race to claim a $10 million Ansari X Prize purse for privately financed flight to the edge of space is heating up.

Growth, Mortality of T. Rex Gets Clearer. Here's a dinosaur finding that parents can appreciate: The teenage Tyrannosaurus rex typically went through an explosive growth spurt, gaining nearly 5 pounds a day.

Space Science Pioneer Van Allen Questions Human Spaceflight. A leading space scientist has called to question the validity of human spaceflight, suggesting that sending astronauts outward from Earth is outdated and too costly.
China Begins Manned Space Flight Countdown. Chinese astronauts are in the final stages of preparing for a manned space mission that will orbit the globe 14 times before returning to Earth.
Sunspot Grows to 20 Times Size of Earth. A sunspot group aimed squarely at Earth has grown to 20 times the size of our planet and has the potential to unleash a major solar storm.

Japanese Lunar Probe Facing Delays. A lunar orbiter that Japan had planned to launch this year could face further delays because of a funding shortfall and problems developing the probe's capabilities.
Pollutants From Asia Appear on East Coast. Scientists looking into air quality and climate change have found pollutants from as far as Asia over New England and the Atlantic.
U.S. Barred From Weakening Dolphin Rules. A federal judge ruled that the Bush administration cannot change the standards commercial fisheries must meet before tuna can carry the dolphin-safe label.
Canadian Robot a Candidate to Save Hubble. NASA said it is moving ahead with plans to send a robot to the rescue of the aging Hubble Space Telescope.

Cave Explorers Discover Pit in Croatia. Cave explorers discovered a pit inside a mountain range in central Croatia believed to have the world's deepest subterranean vertical drop, at nearly 1,700 feet.
Scientists Seek Better Way to Measure Rain. Meteorologists at North Carolina State University are working on a way to more accurately measure rainfall in small areas.

Private Rocket Explodes in Washington State. A team taking a low-budget stab at the $10 million Ansari X Prize suffered a setback when their rocket malfunctioned and exploded after shooting less than 1,000 feet.
Southeast Coast Sees Fewer Turtle Nests. About half the usual number of loggerhead turtles have nested between North Carolina and Florida this season, and scientists have no explanation for the drop.
Company Said to Be Ready to Clone Pets. A company that unveiled the world's first cloned cat nearly three years ago now says it is ready to start filling orders for cloned pets.
Deep-Sea Vessel Puts Ocean Floor in Reach. A new deep-sea research vessel will be able to carry people to 99 percent of the ocean floor, diving deeper than the famed Alvin.
Chorus Frog Found Croaking in Virginia. The Southern chorus frog has been found in southeastern Virginia, far outside its previously known range.
Expedition to Probe Gulf of Mexico. Scientists will use advanced technology never before deployed beneath the sea to discover new creatures in the Gulf of Mexico's deepest reaches.
New Method May Predict Quakes Weeks Ahead. Swedish geologists may have found a way to predict earthquakes weeks before they happen by monitoring metals in subsoil water near earthquake sites.
Marine Expedition Finds New Species. Norwegian scientists explored the deep waters of the Atlantic Ocean and their findings include what appear to be new species of fish and squid.
Annual Study Finds Rise in Beach Closures. The number of days that beaches closed or posted warnings because of pollution rose sharply in 2003 due to more rainfall and tougher standards.
Pacific May Be Seeing New El Nino. Warming water temperatures in the central equatorial Pacific last month may indicate the start of a new El Nino.
Cassini Spacecraft Sees Saturn Lightning. The Cassini spacecraft's mission to Saturn has revealed a new radiation belt and found that lightning in its atmosphere is occurring in different patterns.

Poachers Putting Endangered Rhinos at Risk. Gangs of poachers in Congo have been slaughtering the world's population of northern white rhinos, reducing the population by about one-half in just over a year.
Experts Downplay Texas Shark Attacks. Three shark attacks off the Texas coast in the past two months are unusual but don't mean there are more sharks than normal, marine biologists say.
Canadian Team Joins Rocket Launch Contest. The $10 million competition to send a private manned rocket into space started looking more like a race when a Canadian team announced launch plans.
Universities to Build Largest Telescope. The University of Texas and Texas A&M are planning to construct what they call the world's largest telescope.
E-mail scam targets police chief. Wiltshire Police warns about phishing after its fraud squad chief was targeted by an email scam.
Card fraud unit nets 36,000 cards. In its first two years, the UK's dedicated card fraud unit has recovered 36,000 stolen cards and made 171 arrests.
Super ant colony hits Australia. A giant 100km colony of ants discovered in Melbourne, Australia, could threaten local insect species.
Teenage T. rex's monster growth. Tyrannosaurus rex achieved its massive size due to an enormous growth spurt during its adolescent years.
Scientists Discover Ganymede has a Lumpy Interior. Scientists have discovered irregular lumps beneath the icy surface of Jupiter's largest moon, Ganymede.
Mars Rovers Relay Images Through Mars Express. ESA's Mars Express has relayed pictures from one of NASA's Mars rovers for the first time, as part of interplanetary networking demonstrations.
Storage, servers bruise HP earnings. Earnings per share rise compared with a year ago, but Hewlett-Packard misses analysts' expectations by a long shot.
IBM to hire even more new workers. By the end of the year, the computing giant plans to have its biggest headcount since 1991.
IBM Chips May Someday Heal Themselves. New technology applies electrical fuses to help identify and repair faults in IBM's chip designs.
Wireless net to get speed boost. Wireless computer networks could soon be running 10 times faster than they do now.
GameBoy mini-games win prize. A set of GameBoy micro-games is named as the most innovative game of the year at a festival in Scotland.
Microsoft takes down SP2 sharers. Microsoft is stopping people getting hold of a key security update via net-based file-sharing systems.
Long-awaited Doom 3 hits the UK. Doom 3 goes on sale in the UK at a time of renewed concerns over violence in video games.
Britons embrace digital lifestyle. People in the UK are spending more time and money going digital, says communications watchdog Ofcom.
PlayStation potential to learning. The PlayStation games console could be developed into a learning tool for children, says a Northumberland head teacher.
'Invisible' technology for Olympics. Getting the technology in place for Athens 2004 is an Olympic task in itself.
Satellite boosts Olympic security. An enhanced satellite location system aims to help Olympic security guards react more quickly to emergencies.
3D holograms to crack forgeries. A 3D hologram technique could transform how experts spot forged signatures and other handwritten documents.
Cassini Spies Two Little Saturn Moons. NASA's Cassini spacecraft has spied two new little moons around satellite-rich Saturn.
Nobel Laureate Decries Stem Cell Limits. A Nobel laureate in medicine said the Bush administration's limits on embryonic stem cell research have effectively stopped the clock on scientists' efforts.
Vodafone Peddles New BlackBerry. Research In Motion's BlackBerry 7100v, sporting the company's latest keyboard technology, is being offered exclusively through Vodafone.
Large piece of space shuttle Columbia found. A 1.8-metre-long piece of the space shuttle Columbia was recently found in Texas. The shuttle broke up over the state on Feb. 1, 2003.
Kodak, IBM team up to build image sensors. The two companies zoom in on semiconductor technology to help digital cameras and camera phones take better pictures.
Hackers Jump On Reported Windows Flaws. Less than a day after Microsoft detailed the latest Windows vulnerability, hackers were hunting for exploit codes.
Airespace partners with IBM on Wi-Fi service. Airespace Inc., a Silicon Valley telecommunications start-up, won a partnership with IBM to grab a piece of the growing Wi-Fi market.
EarthLink tests file-sharing program. A new file-sharing program hit the Net, posted by Internet service provider EarthLink on a corner of the company's research and development site.
AOL Dumps Microsoft's Sender ID. America Online's announcement that it would abandon Microsoft's Sender ID e-mail authentication standard is a serious setback for the Redmond company.
Mouse for the nose. Canadian inventor Dmitry Gorodnichy has devised the world's first computer to be controlled by the nose and eyelids, a boon for people with disabilities.
XM Radio Goes Online. XM Satellite Radio is the latest content provider to join the increasingly crowded online-music market with a service delivering radio programming via the Internet.
RIM takes new BlackBerry design overseas. Research In Motion is targeting European and Asian markets with a phone-and-messaging device that uses the company's new SureType keyboard design.
Internet Explorer Loses More Market Share. New data shows Web site visitors paying more attention to alternative browsers, as Microsoft's share drops to 93 percent.
Apple accused of ripping-off Britain. The Office of Fair Trading in the UK has not taken up the request that Apple is ripping-off UK music lovers with higher download prices.
Intel Delays Launch of Projection TV Chip. Semiconductor giant Intel Corp. said it won't be offering a chip for projection TVs by the end of 2004 as it had announced earlier.
